Driven by a storm, a ship's neglected spine snaps on a reef, and the sea claims her sailors' souls. The rotten timbers of a tenement finally give way, and dozens are buried alive. An old levee breaks, and a wall of water gushes forth to sweep away whole neighborhoods. Calamity gremlins are the architects of countless preventable disasters. When bridges fall, walls crumble, and wells collapse, calamity gremlins cackle with glee.

While most gremlins prefer to do their own work, calamity gremlins prefer to deceive and manipulate others. They bribe inspectors to look the other way, con their way into secure locations, and sabotage blueprints and communications for complicated infrastructure projects. Wherever they go, they use their expertise in both physical and social destruction to do maximum harm. Their true joy lies in getting others to cause tragedies, but they happily bring about disasters for their own amusement.

Calamity gremlins see weaker gremlins as useful pawns in their schemes. Gremlins who hope to achieve greatness at the side of a calamity should take care, however, as their sadistic and capricious leaders might engineer their demise for amusement.

Enemy Among Us

Of the many tools calamity gremlins have in their ruinous toolboxes, their favorite is their ability to steal the guise of another person. It's difficult to complete a project when anyone you see could be an impostor aiming to sabotage it. To a calamity gremlin, the ultimate accomplishment is to direct mistrust toward a project's most able leader, which can lead to their removal and replacement with incompetent leadership.

You conjure a spike that thrusts up from the earth beneath a target creature, potentially impaling it. The spike is made of cold iron and deals 8d6 piercing damage. The target must attempt a Reflex save.

Critical Success The target dodges the spike and is unaffected.

Success The target is struck by the spike and takes half damage.

Failure The target is impaled through a leg or another nonvital body part. The creature takes full damage and, if it's standing on solid ground, becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.eIcWbB5o3pP6OIMe]{Immobilized}. It can attempt to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.SkZAQRkLLkmBQNB9]{Escape} (the DC is your spell DC). While it remains impaled, it takes damage from any weakness to cold iron it has at the end of each of its turns.

Critical Failure As failure, but the creature is impaled through a vital organ or its center of mass, taking double damage, and it is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.AJh5ex99aV6VTggg]{Off-Guard} as long as it's impaled.

Heightened (+1) The damage increases by 2d6.

You conjure a spectral scythe that gradually phases into reality above a target's head and follows them wherever they go. At the end of the creature's next three turns, an ominous bell tolls, and the creature must succeed at a Will save or be @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 1} (@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 2} on a critical failure); this effect has the emotion, fear, and mental traits. After the third toll, the scythe swings, striking the creature in the neck and dealing 10d10 slashing damage with a basic Fortitude save. If the spell reduces a target to 0 Hit Points, they die; this is a death effect.

Heightened (+1) Increase the damage by 2d10.

Requirements You can bleed.

Trigger A creature deals piercing, slashing, or persistent bleed damage to you.

You curse the target, punishing it for having the audacity to spill your blood. The target takes 2d6 persistent bleed damage and must attempt a Will save.

Critical Success The target is unaffected.

Success The target takes half the persistent bleed damage.

Failure The target takes the full persistent bleed damage. Until the bleeding stops, the target has weakness 1 to piercing and slashing damage. @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spell-effects.Item.buXx8Azr4BYWPtFg]{Spell Effect: Blood Vendetta (Failure)}

Critical Failure As failure, but the target takes double the persistent bleed damage.

Heightened (+2) The persistent bleed damage increases by 2d6.

You force the target to see a vision of its own death. It takes 8d6 mental damage with a Will save. If the target is reduced to 0 HP by this spell, its vision becomes reality and kills it instantly.

Critical Success The target is unaffected.

Success The target takes half damage and is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 1}.

Failure The target takes full damage and is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 2}.

Critical Failure The target takes double damage, is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 4} and is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.sDPxOjQ9kx2RZE8D]{Fleeing} for as long as it's frightened.

Heightened (+1) The damage increases by 2d6.

Area 30-foot cone or 10-foot emanation

You swing a weapon you're holding, and the weapon magically multiplies into duplicates that swipe at all creatures in either a cone or an emanation. This flurry deals four dice of damage to creatures in the area. This damage has the same type as the weapon and uses the same die size. Determine the die size as if you were attacking with the weapon; for instance, if you were wielding a two-hand weapon in both hands, you'd use its two-hand damage die.

Critical Success The creature is unaffected.

Success The target takes half damage.

Failure The target takes full damage.

Critical Failure The target takes double damage and is subject to the weapon's critical specialization effect.

Heightened (+1) Add another damage die.

The simplest magic does your bidding. You can perform simple magical effects for as long as you Sustain the spell. Each time you Sustain the spell, you can choose one of four options.

  • Cook Cool, warm, or flavor 1 pound of nonliving material.
  • Lift Slowly lift an unattended object of light Bulk or less 1 foot off the ground.
  • Make Create a temporary object of negligible Bulk, made of congealed magical substance. The object looks crude and artificial and is extremely fragile-it can't be used as a tool, weapon, or locus or cost for a spell.
  • Tidy Color, clean, or soil an object of light Bulk or less. You can affect an object of 1 Bulk with 10 rounds of concentration, and a larger object at 1 minute per Bulk.

Prestidigitation can't deal damage or cause adverse conditions. Any actual change to an object (beyond what is noted above) persists only as long as you Sustain the spell.

An infiltrator thieves' toolkit add a +1 item bonus to checks to Pick Locks and Disable Devices.

If your thieves' toolkit is broken, you can repair it by replacing the lock picks with @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-srd.Item.BznmPaRjI4Orb0IH]{Replacement Picks} appropriate to your tools; this doesn't require using the Repair action. If you wear your thieves' toolkit, you can draw and replace it as part of the action that uses it.
These blades come in a variety of shapes and styles, but they are typically 2 feet long.
This weapon has a wooden shaft ending in a large, heavy metal head. The head of the hammer might be single-sided or double-sided, but it's always capable of delivering powerful bludgeoning blows.
The calamity gremlin deals an additional 3d6 precision damage to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.AJh5ex99aV6VTggg]{Off-Guard} creatures.
The calamity gremlin Strides up to half their Speed and attempts a @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.QNAVeNKtHA0EUw4X]{Feint}, in either order.

The calamity gremlin makes two warhammer Strikes against a wall, ceiling, or floor in reach. The object's Hardness is halved for the purpose of determining the damage from these Strikes, and it applies only once after combining the damage from both Strikes. If the calamity gremlin brings a wall's Hit Points to zero, they can take a free Step or Stride through the breach.

The calamity gremlin can take on the appearance of any Small or Medium humanoid. This doesn't change their Speed or their attack and damage modifiers with their Strikes, but it might change the damage type their Strikes deal (typically to bludgeoning).

Frequency Once per month

Effect The calamity gremlin spends 8 hours laying a terrible curse upon area with a radius of up to 100 feet. The curse triggers between one day and one year later at a time set during its creation and results in some kind of violent misfortune, such as an exploding cannon or a collapsing bridge. The exact effects are up to the GM. Typically, the curse creates a hazard of up to 7th level. If the calamity gremlin is interrupted while laying the curse, their magic is still expended, preventing them from using calamity again for 1 month. A calamity gremlin can only have one calamity active at a time; creating a new calamity automatically ends the curse on any previously affected location. A calamity gremlin who appears to perish as a result of their own calamity curse emerges [[/gmr 2d4 #days]]{2d4 days} later, having somehow survived.
